metadata.description: One-shot deployment of the Microsoft Defender for Office 365 hunting pack: 21 hunting queries (savedSearches) + 5 scheduled analytic rules. Use 'deployAnalyticRulesEnabled' to choose whether the analytic rules deploy enabled or disabled.
Microsoft Sentinel Log Analytics workspace name
User choice for the initial state of every deployed analytic rule: true = deploy ENABLED (default), false = deploy DISABLED for a staged rollout / review before incidents are generated.

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Malicious Email Delivered to Inbox (Block Failure)
properties.query:
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware")
| where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
| where DeliveryLocation in ("Inbox/folder", "Inbox")
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress,
          Subject, ThreatTypes, ThreatNames, DetectionMethods,
          DeliveryLocation, LatestDeliveryLocation
| sort by Timestamp desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Surfaces emails that carried a Phish/Malware verdict yet were still delivered to the user's Inbox - the highest residual-risk point in Defender for Office 365. Each row is a malicious message sitting in a mailbox. Value: demonstrates MDO effectiveness and

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Phishing Campaign Clustering
properties.query:
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ThreatTypes has "Phish"
| summarize
    Recipients = dcount(RecipientEmailAddress),
    Messages   = count(),
    Senders    = make_set(SenderFromAddress, 15),
    Delivered  = countif(DeliveryAction == "Delivered"),
    FirstSeen  = min(Timestamp),
    LastSeen   = max(Timestamp)
    by Subject, SenderFromDomain
| where Recipients >= 5
| sort by Recipients desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Groups similar phishing messages (subject + sender domain) to move from "one email" to "a campaign" and size the blast radius. Prioritise clusters where Delivered > 0. Value: turns isolated detections into campaign-level situational awareness. Triage: a s

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Confirmed Malware Attachments
properties.query:
EmailAttachmentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ThreatTypes has "Malware"
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress,
          FileName, FileType, SHA256, ThreatNames, DetectionMethods, FileSize
| sort by Timestamp desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Lists email attachments with a confirmed Malware verdict. Each SHA256 is a pivot point into endpoint telemetry to confirm whether the file executed. Value: bridges MDO (mail) to MDE (endpoint). Triage: pivot each SHA256 to DeviceFileEvents / DeviceProcess

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Dangerous File Types Delivered
properties.query:
let RiskyTypes = dynamic(["exe","scr","js","vbs","ps1","lnk","iso","img","hta","cmd","bat","wsf","jar","one"]);
EmailAttachmentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileType in~ (RiskyTypes)
    or FileName has_any (".exe",".scr",".js",".lnk",".iso",".img",".hta",".one",".vbs")
| join kind=inner (
    EmailEvents
    | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
    | project NetworkMessageId, DeliveryLocation, Subject, EmailDirection
) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, FileName, FileType,
          Subject, DeliveryLocation, EmailDirection, SHA256
| sort by Timestamp desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Detects high-risk attachment extensions that reached the mailbox even without a threat verdict (evasion / zero-day). Container formats (iso, img, lnk, one) are common evasion vectors. Value: catches malicious delivery that slipped past verdict-based block

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Safe Links Click-Through to Blocked URL
properties.query:
UrlClickEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "ClickAllowed" or IsClickedThrough != ""
| where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware")
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, ThreatTypes, DetectionMethods,
          IPAddress, IsClickedThrough, Workload, NetworkMessageId
| sort by Timestamp desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: High-value MDO use case: users who, despite the Safe Links warning page, chose to continue to a malicious link. Each click-through user is a compromise candidate. Value: identifies real user exposure that survived a protective control. Triage: review each

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Users Who Clicked Later-Confirmed Malicious Mail
properties.query:
let MaliciousMail =
    EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware")
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, ThreatTypes;
UrlClickEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| join kind=inner MaliciousMail on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, Subject, ThreatTypes, IsClickedThrough,
          IPAddress, Workload
| sort by Timestamp desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Correlates EmailEvents (verdict) with UrlClickEvents (click) to find real exposure: users who clicked a link in a message that was (or later became) Phish/Malware. Value: turns a campaign into a concrete victim list. Triage: prioritise credential reset an

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Email Auth Failures (SPF/DKIM/DMARC Spoofing)
properties.query:
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| extend Auth = parse_json(AuthenticationDetails)
| extend SPF = tostring(Auth.SPF), DKIM = tostring(Auth.DKIM),
         DMARC = tostring(Auth.DMARC), CompAuth = tostring(Auth.CompAuth)
| where DMARC == "fail" or (SPF == "fail" and DKIM == "fail")
| summarize Messages = count(),
            Recipients = dcount(RecipientEmailAddress),
            Delivered = countif(DeliveryAction == "Delivered")
    by SenderFromDomain, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, CompAuth
| where Delivered > 0
| sort by Messages desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Detects impersonation of trusted domains via inbound email authentication results. DMARC failures on delivered mail claiming to be from your own or partner domains are strong spoofing / BEC indicators. Value: exposes domain spoofing that reached mailboxes

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - BEC Display-Name Impersonation
properties.query:
let Execs = dynamic(["CEO Name","CFO Name","Managing Director"]);
let CorpDomains = dynamic(["contoso.com","contoso.es"]);
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| where SenderDisplayName has_any (Execs)
| where not(SenderFromDomain in~ (CorpDomains))
| project Timestamp, SenderDisplayName, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
          RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation
| sort by Timestamp desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Detects inbound emails whose display name imitates an executive but whose sender domain is NOT corporate - the classic CEO-fraud / BEC pattern. Customise the Execs and CorpDomains lists before operationalising. Triage: an exec display name from gmail / lo

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Lookalike / Typosquatting Domains in URLs
properties.query:
let Brand = "contoso";
let LegitSuffix = "contoso.com";
EmailUrlInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where UrlDomain has Brand and UrlDomain !endswith LegitSuffix
| summarize Messages = dcount(NetworkMessageId), Urls = make_set(Url, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by UrlDomain
| sort by Messages desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Attackers register domains that resemble your brand. This query surfaces typosquatting / lookalike domains embedded in email URLs (e.g. contoso-support.com, cont0so.com, contoso.secure-login.net). Customise Brand and the legitimate-domain suffix. Triage:

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - ZAP Gaps - Threats Detected After Delivery
properties.query:
EmailPostDeliveryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Action has "ZAP" or ActionType has "ZAP"
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress, Action, ActionType,
          ActionTrigger, ActionResult, DeliveryLocation, ThreatTypes
| sort by Timestamp desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: EmailPostDeliveryEvents shows which already-delivered emails were pulled by Zero-hour Auto Purge (ZAP) - and, crucially, which ones could NOT be removed. Value: exposes residual risk where ZAP failed. Triage: focus on ActionResult != "Success" - malicious

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Exposure Window - Delivery to Remediation
properties.query:
let Delivered =
    EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d) and ThreatTypes != ""
    | project NetworkMessageId, DeliveredTime = Timestamp, RecipientEmailAddress,
              Subject, ThreatTypes;
EmailPostDeliveryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| join kind=inner Delivered on NetworkMessageId
| extend ExposureMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, DeliveredTime)
| where ExposureMinutes >= 0
| project DeliveredTime, RemediatedTime = Timestamp, ExposureMinutes,
          RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, ThreatTypes, Action, ActionResult
| sort by ExposureMinutes desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Computes how long a malicious email sat in the mailbox before it was removed - a direct KPI for MDO effectiveness and SOC response time. Value: quantifies dwell time of malicious mail; great leadership metric. Triage: long exposure windows (hours/days) in

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Quishing (QR Phishing) and Suspicious Images
properties.query:
EmailAttachmentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileType in~ ("png","jpg","jpeg","gif","bmp","svg")
| join kind=inner (
    EmailEvents
    | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
    | where UrlCount <= 1
    | where ThreatTypes has "Phish" or DetectionMethods has_any ("Spoof","Impersonation")
    | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, DeliveryAction
) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, FileName, FileType,
          Subject, DeliveryAction
| sort by Timestamp desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: QR-code phishing evades URL analysis by embedding the link inside an image attachment. This query finds inbound mail carrying an image with few/no analysable URLs and phishing / impersonation signals. Triage: an image-only email with a credential/MFA them

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Compromised Internal Sender (Intra-Org Phishing)
properties.query:
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where EmailDirection == "Intra-org"
| where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware")
| summarize Recipients = dcount(RecipientEmailAddress),
            Messages   = count(),
            Subjects   = make_set(Subject, 10),
            FirstSeen  = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen   = max(Timestamp)
    by SenderFromAddress
| where Recipients >= 3
| sort by Recipients desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: A malicious email sent from INSIDE the org usually means a compromised account used for lateral phishing. Flags internal senders pushing Phish/Malware to several colleagues. Value: early signal of account takeover being weaponised for internal spread. Tri

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Malicious Campaign Overview (EmailClusterId)
properties.query:
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where isnotempty(EmailClusterId)
| where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware")
| summarize
    Messages    = count(),
    Recipients  = dcount(RecipientEmailAddress),
    Delivered   = countif(DeliveryAction == "Delivered"),
    Blocked     = countif(DeliveryAction == "Blocked"),
    Senders     = make_set(SenderFromAddress, 15),
    Subjects    = make_set(Subject, 10),
    ThreatMix   = make_set(ThreatTypes, 10),
    Detections  = make_set(DetectionMethods, 10),
    FirstSeen   = min(Timestamp),
    LastSeen    = max(Timestamp)
    by EmailClusterId
| where Recipients >= 5
| extend DeliveredRatio = round(todouble(Delivered) / Messages, 2)
| sort by Recipients desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Reconstructs malicious mail campaigns directly from EmailEvents using Defender's own EmailClusterId, so it works regardless of CampaignInfo availability. Aggregates each cluster's reach, delivery success and threat mix. Value: campaign-level view (who/wha

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Campaign View via CampaignInfo

tags.name: description
tags.value: Reads Defender for Office 365 curated Campaign Views from the CampaignInfo Advanced Hunting table to list active malicious campaigns targeting the tenant. IMPORTANT: CampaignInfo is a newer/evolving MDO table and its columns can vary by tenant/ring. Run `

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Campaign Exposure (Delivered + Clicked)
properties.query:
let Campaigns =
    EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where isnotempty(EmailClusterId)
    | where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware")
    | project NetworkMessageId, EmailClusterId, Subject, ThreatTypes, RecipientEmailAddress;
UrlClickEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| join kind=inner Campaigns on NetworkMessageId
| summarize
    Clicks       = count(),
    ClickThrough = countif(IsClickedThrough != "" and IsClickedThrough != "0"),
    Victims      = dcount(AccountUpn),
    VictimList   = make_set(AccountUpn, 40),
    Urls         = make_set(Url, 10),
    LastClick    = max(Timestamp)
    by EmailClusterId, ThreatTypes
| sort by Victims desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Joins malicious campaign clusters (EmailClusterId) to Safe Links clicks to reveal the campaigns that not only landed but were actually clicked - the campaigns with real, human exposure. Triage: these clusters are the priority for user reset/awareness. The

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Teams Safe Links Click-Through
properties.query:
UrlClickEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Workload == "Microsoft Teams" or Workload has "Teams"
| where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware") or IsClickedThrough != ""
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, ThreatTypes, DetectionMethods,
          IPAddress, IsClickedThrough, Workload
| sort by Timestamp desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: UrlClickEvents also records Safe Links clicks inside Microsoft Teams (Workload == "Microsoft Teams"). This finds users who clicked - or clicked through a warning to - a malicious link in Teams. Value: Teams is increasingly abused for phishing that bypasse

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Malicious Files in SharePoint / OneDrive
properties.query:
// Validate columns first:  FileMaliciousContentInfo | getschema
FileMaliciousContentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| sort by Timestamp desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Defender for Office 365 (Safe Attachments for SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams) flags malicious files stored in collaboration. FileMaliciousContentInfo surfaces those detections. IMPORTANT: run `FileMaliciousContentInfo | getschema` to confirm columns (expe

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Mass File Download / Exfil After Phishing Click
properties.query:
let Clickers =
    UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(3d)
    | where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware")
    | summarize ClickTime = min(Timestamp) by AccountUpn
    | where isnotempty(AccountUpn);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(3d)
| where ActionType in ("FileDownloaded", "FileSyncDownloadedFull", "FileAccessed")
| where Application has_any ("SharePoint", "OneDrive")
| extend Upn = tolower(AccountDisplayName)
| join kind=inner (Clickers | extend Upn = tolower(AccountUpn)) on Upn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 6h)
| summarize Downloads = count(),
            Files = dcount(ObjectName),
            Apps = make_set(Application, 5),
            IPs = make_set(IPAddress, 10),
            FirstDownload = min(Timestamp),
            LastDownload = max(Timestamp)
    by AccountUpn, ClickTime
| where Downloads >= 50
| sort by Downloads desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Correlates users who clicked a malicious link (UrlClickEvents) with a subsequent burst of SharePoint/OneDrive file downloads (CloudAppEvents) - a classic post-compromise collection/exfiltration pattern. Triage: a spike of FileDownloaded / FileSyncDownload

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Suspicious Inbox Rule After Phishing Click
properties.query:
let Clickers =
    UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(3d)
    | where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware") or IsClickedThrough != ""
    | summarize ClickTime = min(Timestamp) by AccountUpn
    | where isnotempty(AccountUpn);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(3d)
| where ActionType in ("New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule", "UpdateInboxRules")
| extend Rule = tostring(RawEventData.Parameters)
| where Rule has_any ("ForwardTo", "RedirectTo", "ForwardAsAttachmentTo",
                      "DeleteMessage", "MarkAsRead", "MoveToFolder")
| extend Upn = tolower(AccountDisplayName)
| join kind=inner (Clickers | extend Upn = tolower(AccountUpn)) on Upn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 6h)
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, ClickTime, ActionType, Rule, IPAddress, Application
| sort by Timestamp desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: A hallmark of Business Email Compromise: shortly after a user clicks a malicious link, an inbox rule is created that forwards, redirects, deletes or marks-as-read mail (to hide the attacker's activity). Correlates UrlClickEvents with CloudAppEvents inbox-

properties.displayName: MDO Hunting - Kill Chain - Email to Click to Identity to Cloud
properties.query:
let lookback = 7d;
let malicious =
    EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware") and DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, ThreatTypes;
let clicks =
    UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | join kind=inner malicious on NetworkMessageId
    | summarize ClickTime = min(Timestamp), Url = any(Url), Subject = any(Subject),
                ThreatTypes = any(ThreatTypes) by AccountUpn
    | where isnotempty(AccountUpn);
let cloud =
    CloudAppEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where ActionType in ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","UpdateInboxRules",
                           "FileDownloaded","FileSyncDownloadedFull",
                           "Consent to application","Add-MailboxPermission")
    | summarize CloudActions = make_set(ActionType, 10), CloudActivityTime = min(Timestamp)
            by Upn = tolower(AccountDisplayName);
clicks
| extend Upn = tolower(AccountUpn)
| join kind=leftouter cloud on Upn
| extend Stage = case(
      isnotempty(CloudActivityTime), "4-CloudActivity (contain now)",
      "3-Clicked (identity-risk review)")
| project AccountUpn, ClickTime, Subject, ThreatTypes, Url,
          CloudActions, CloudActivityTime, Stage
| sort by Stage desc, ClickTime desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Reconstructs the full phishing kill chain across products: a malicious email that was delivered (MDO) -> the user clicked (Safe Links) -> a risky/successful sign-in followed (Entra) -> post-compromise cloud activity (inbox rule, download, consent). One ro

properties.displayName: MDO - Safe Links Click-Through to Malicious URL
properties.description:
Fires when a user clicks (or clicks through the warning page to) a URL that Defender for
Office 365 Safe Links classified as Phish or Malware. Each hit is a high-confidence
compromise candidate. Low noise because the verdict is confirmed. Promoted from hunting
query MDO-05. MITRE ATT&CK: T1566 (Phishing), T1204.001 (Malicious Link).
properties.query:
UrlClickEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| where ActionType == "ClickAllowed" or (isnotempty(IsClickedThrough) and IsClickedThrough != "0")
| where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware")
| where isnotempty(AccountUpn)
| project Timestamp, ReportId, AccountUpn, Url, ThreatTypes, DetectionMethods,
          IPAddress, IsClickedThrough, Workload, NetworkMessageId

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{AccountUpn}} clicked a {{ThreatTypes}} URL protected by Safe Links from {{IPAddress}}. Treat as a compromise candidate: review sign-ins and reset credentials.

properties.displayName: MDO - BEC Display-Name Impersonation of Executive
properties.description:
Fires when an inbound email uses an executive's display name but originates from a
non-corporate sender domain - the classic CEO-fraud / BEC pattern. Customise the Execs and
CorpDomains lists before enabling. Promoted from hunting query MDO-08.
MITRE ATT&CK: T1566 (Phishing).
properties.query:
let Execs = dynamic(["CEO Name","CFO Name","Managing Director"]);
let CorpDomains = dynamic(["contoso.com","contoso.es"]);
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| where SenderDisplayName has_any (Execs)
| where not(SenderFromDomain in~ (CorpDomains))
| project Timestamp, ReportId, SenderDisplayName, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
          RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, NetworkMessageId

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: Inbound mail to {{RecipientEmailAddress}} spoofs executive display name '{{SenderDisplayName}}' from non-corporate domain {{SenderFromDomain}}. Verify out-of-band before any financial action.

properties.displayName: MDO - Compromised Internal Sender (Intra-Org Phishing)
properties.description:
Fires when an internal mailbox sends Phish/Malware to 3 or more colleagues within the
window - a strong account-takeover signal being weaponised for lateral phishing. Promoted
from hunting query MDO-13. MITRE ATT&CK: T1534 (Internal Spearphishing), T1566 (Phishing).
properties.query:
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(3h)
| where EmailDirection == "Intra-org"
| where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware")
| summarize
    Recipients = dcount(RecipientEmailAddress),
    Messages   = count(),
    Subjects   = make_set(Subject, 8),
    ThreatMix  = make_set(ThreatTypes, 5),
    ReportId   = take_any(ReportId),
    Timestamp  = min(Timestamp)
    by SenderFromAddress
| where Recipients >= 3

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{SenderFromAddress}} sent {{Messages}} malicious intra-org messages to {{Recipients}} colleagues. Likely compromised - reset credentials and revoke sessions.

properties.displayName: MDO - Suspicious Inbox Rule After Phishing Click
properties.description:
Fires when a user who recently clicked a malicious link then creates an inbox rule that
forwards, redirects, deletes or hides mail - a hallmark of Business Email Compromise.
Correlates UrlClickEvents with CloudAppEvents inbox-rule operations. Promoted from hunting
query MDO-25. MITRE ATT&CK: T1114 (Email Collection), T1564 (Hide Artifacts).
properties.query:
let Clickers =
    UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(3h)
    | where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware") or (isnotempty(IsClickedThrough) and IsClickedThrough != "0")
    | summarize ClickTime = min(Timestamp) by AccountUpn
    | where isnotempty(AccountUpn);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(3h)
| where ActionType in ("New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule", "UpdateInboxRules")
| extend Rule = tostring(RawEventData.Parameters)
| where Rule has_any ("ForwardTo", "RedirectTo", "ForwardAsAttachmentTo", "DeleteMessage", "MarkAsRead", "MoveToFolder")
| extend Upn = tolower(AccountDisplayName)
| join kind=inner (Clickers | extend Upn = tolower(AccountUpn)) on Upn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 6h)
| project Timestamp, ReportId, AccountUpn, ClickTime, ActionType, Rule, IPAddress

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: Inbox rule created by {{AccountUpn}} after malicious click
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{AccountUpn}} created inbox rule '{{ActionType}}' shortly after clicking a malicious link (from {{IPAddress}}). Strong BEC / account-takeover signal - remove the rule and contain the identity.

properties.displayName: MDO - Illicit OAuth App Consent (Consent Phishing)
properties.description:
Fires when a user grants delegated consent to an OAuth application - the key event in
consent-phishing / illicit-grant attacks that give an attacker persistent access to mail
and files. Review the app, publisher and scopes. Promoted from hunting query MDO-26.
MITRE ATT&CK: T1528 (Steal Application Access Token), T1566 (Phishing).
properties.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application", "Add delegated permission grant")
| extend AppName = tostring(RawEventData.ObjectName)
| project Timestamp, ReportId, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActionType, AppName,
          IPAddress, IsAdminOperation, UserAgent

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{AccountDisplayName}} granted OAuth consent to app '{{AppName}}' from {{IPAddress}}. Review publisher and scopes; revoke if illicit (consent-phishing persistence).
